title: Why is the q=1 AMW ring chain irreducible with positive normalization?
question: The AMW q=1 theorem asserts that on the ring sector S_n(\lambda) with x_i>0 and 0\le t<1 the inhomogeneous multispecies exclusion chain has stationary law \pi(\eta)=F_{\eta}(x;1,t)/P_{\lambda}(x;1,t), where P_{\lambda}(x;1,t)=\sum_{\nu\in S_n(\lambda)}F_{\nu}(x;1,t). However, the proof sketch in node p3-s4 assumes the process is irreducible on that sector and that the normalization sum is strictly positive without giving details. How can we check irreducibility of the q=1 ring chain and verify that the sector sum P_{\lambda}(x;1,t) is finite and positive, thereby justifying the use of the AMW stationary distribution?
